messages.content: We discussed the room layout, and I’m ready to compare Hotel Folly with the city-side option one last time. Please rebuild both six-night totals, including every required charge, and make sure either room really accepts two adults and our 14-year-old.

I’ll separate required lodging charges from meals and driving estimates. What are the latest figures for the city-side property? I still have Hotel Folly’s earlier $1,977.36 quote, but that needs to be reconciled with the updated parking and breakfast terms.

The city-side quote is $1,898.70 after tax, with free parking and breakfast. It wants half up front. The room is listed as one king and one full sleeper sofa. Hotel Folly now says the resort fee is in the quoted total, but parking is $30 a night and breakfast is separate.

Then Hotel Folly’s mandatory total is $2,157.36: $1,977.36 for the room, taxes, and resort fee, plus $180 for six nights of parking. The city-side property remains $1,898.70 because tax, parking, and breakfast are included. Its advance deposit is $949.35, leaving $949.35 due later. Hotel Folly’s stated advance charge is $659.12, with $1,498.24 remaining after parking is added.
Confirm that neither one adds a third-person fee or treats a 14-year-old as another adult.

Both current rate details permit three registered guests. Hotel Folly shows two adults and one child age 14 in a Two Queen Studio, with no extra-person charge. The city-side room also allows three guests and shows the same occupancy, using the king bed and full sleeper sofa; there is no added fee for the teenager. The sleeper sofa is included in the room type, though it would need to be opened each night.
Now compare the driving. We expect three beach days and two days in historic Charleston. We’ll probably stay around the hotel the other day.

From Hotel Folly, the beach days require no driving. Historic Charleston is roughly 25 to 35 minutes each way in ordinary traffic. Two downtown visits would add about $36 in parking and an estimated $14 in fuel, for $50 total. From the city-side hotel, historic Charleston is about 10 minutes away, while the beach is generally 25 to 40 minutes each way. Three beach days would add about $45 in beach parking and roughly $24 in fuel, for $69 total.
So give me the practical totals, with breakfast at Hotel Folly included as an estimate rather than pretending it is mandatory.

Using $18 per person per morning for six mornings, Hotel Folly breakfast would be about $324. Its practical trip total is therefore $2,531.36: $2,157.36 mandatory lodging and parking, $324 breakfast, and $50 for the two historic-district days. The city-side practical total is $1,967.70: $1,898.70 lodging with breakfast and parking included, plus $69 for beach travel. The city-side option is about $563.66 less overall.
Hotel Folly’s room also has the ocean-facing balcony, correct? The city-side room is just a standard window room.
Correct. Hotel Folly’s available Two Queen Studio is explicitly labeled ocean-facing with a private balcony. The city-side king-and-sleeper room has a standard window and no balcony.

For a coastal week where we’ll have real downtime at the hotel, prioritize the balcony when there is one. It is still a preference, not a reason to reject a good property by itself, and a first-floor room without one can work. Here, though, the two real beds and no beach commute also matter.

That makes Hotel Folly the stronger fit despite the higher total. The balcony improves the downtime you expect to spend there, the two queen beds avoid six nights on a sleeper sofa, and three beach days require no driving. The city-side property wins on price, breakfast, and access to historic Charleston, but those savings come with the less comfortable sleeping arrangement and repeated beach trips.
Choose Hotel Folly, but don’t book until you restate exactly what must be verified at checkout. Use the $2,531.36 planning total.

Hotel Folly is selected but remains unbooked for July 12-18. The planning total is $2,531.36 for two adults and one 14-year-old: $1,977.36 room, taxes, and resort fee; $180 parking; an estimated $324 breakfast; and about $50 for two historic Charleston visits. Before payment, verify the Two Queen Studio, all three registered guests with no extra-person fee, ocean-facing private balcony, $2,157.36 mandatory hotel total, $659.12 advance charge, remaining balance, and free cancellation through 6:00 p.m. Eastern on July 7.
